title: Introduce operator claim throttler, KMS delegation path, and chained audit checks
author: Maya Chen
description:
Context: Several enterprise customers requested stronger guardrails for operator-initiated cross-tenant and cross-region operations. The existing RBACv2 bindings and KMS usage controls lacked two features we need for compliance: (1) a rate-based operator claim throttler that prevents a single operator/service principal from performing high-frequency tenant-scoped actions across geozones, and (2) a delegated KMS path that lets per-tenant keys be used via a short-lived delegation token instead of long-lived operator credentials.

This PR implements a conservative, opt-in rollout of both features and wires a chained audit-check pipeline that computes incremental checksums on audit batches to detect missing or reordered audit envelopes. Motivation: reduce blast radius from operator automation bugs, provide a compliance-friendly KMS delegation flow for regulated tenants, and increase audit integrity visibility.

Changes in this PR (summary): adds a new operator claim throttler component (pkg/rbacv2/claim_throttler.go) with pluggable policies; implements a KMS delegation service (pkg/kms/delegator.go) that mints short-lived delegation tokens scoped to a tenant and operation; introduces an audit chaining writer (cmd/audit/chain_writer.go) which appends lightweight checksums to batched audit envelopes and verifies upstream sequencing; updates RBAC policy templates and role mappings to honor throttler verdicts; adds end-to-end integration tests and an operator-facing docs page.

Files of interest: pkg/rbacv2/claim_throttler.go, pkg/kms/delegator.go, internal/auth/claim_evaluator.go (hooked), cmd/audit/chain_writer.go, docs/operator/claim-throttler.md, tests/integration/test-kms-delegation.sh.

Rollout plan: feature-flag gated behind feature.operator_claim_throttle and feature.kms_delegation. Start with shadow mode for 2 weeks in prod (no enforcement, only metrics/audit entries), then opt-in enforcement for Dedicated customers on request. KMS delegation is opt-in per-tenant and requires IAM admin consent. Audit chaining will be enabled for all tenants once observed false-positive rate is below 0.5% over a 3-day sampling window.

Testing: unit tests for throttler policy evaluation and token issuance (pkg/*_test.go), integration tests exercise delegated KMS calls and verify audit chain checks (tests/integration/*). CI: added lint and static checks for new packages.

Backward compatibility and security notes: defaults are non-enforcing. Delegation tokens are short-lived (default 15m) and bound to operation and nonce. Throttler verdicts are computed deterministically from operator principal, tenant id, and policy bucket to avoid nondeterministic enforcement.

Related work: references ENG-5821 (operator rate controls) and ENG-5910 (kms per-tenant delegation). See SUP-3382 for a support ticket describing a customer incident that motivated the audit-chain checks.

Checklist:

- [x] Docs for operators/ent-admins
- [x] Feature flag gating
- [x] Security review (initial, follow-up scheduled)

review_comments: Noah Patel: Please add a circuit-breaker for the delegator in case of KMS provider latency spikes. Also add metrics for token issuance latency.
Maya Chen: Added a simple fallback circuit and Prometheus counters; moved token signing to a background worker to reduce hot-path latency (see commit 9d4f2c8 and e4f0a44).
Aisha Khan: Throttler looks good. Suggest tightening default policy for cross-region operator actions from 100/min to 20/min for the initial enforcement phase.
Maya Chen: Reduced default cross-region bucket to 20/min and documented in docs/operator/claim-throttler.md.
Luis Ortega: Audit chaining implementation is fine; can you ensure the checksum algorithm is stable across minor language versions? Prefer using SHA256 with explicit salt/version bytes.
Maya Chen: Switched to SHA256 with explicit version byte and added a migration path for older envelopes (chain_writer.go).

release_notes: Add opt-in operator claim throttling and per-tenant KMS delegation with chained audit checks. Feature gated and disabled by default. See docs/operator/claim-throttler.md for admin configuration.
notes_for_ops: Enable feature.operator_claim_throttle=shadow to validate for two weeks. For Dedicated customers requesting enforcement, set to enforcing per-tenant via admin UI and ensure KMS-delegation is provisioned with IAM consent. Monitor metric operator_claim_throttle.denied and audit.chain.checks_failed.
changelog_entry: security: introduce operator claim throttler and opt-in KMS delegation + audit chaining (feature-flagged)
observable_changes: New metrics: operator_claim_throttle.allowed, operator_claim_throttle.denied, kms_delegation.issue_latency_seconds, audit_chain.verify_failures_count
deploy_instructions: 1) Deploy binary with feature flags off. 2) Enable shadow mode: feature.operator_claim_throttle=shadow, feature.kms_delegation=shadow. 3) After 14 days and acceptable metrics, opt-in tenants individually for enforcement.
post_merge_actions: Create a follow-up ticket to add RBAC policy generator templates for the new throttler buckets (ENG-5992). Schedule compliance comms for tenants that opt into enforced delegation.
external_impact: Customers will see new audit-chain fields in audit envelopes when audit chaining is enabled; default flow is non-enforcing so no behavior change until opt-in.
